title: Rabies Requires Proof, Quarantine, and Dog-Trade Abolition by 2030
excerpt: No incident record supports a fabricated raid story. Verified rabies science still demands urgent exposure care, transparent transport controls, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
One fact needs no dramatization: once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Any possible exposure demands wound washing with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, followed by urgent medical assessment for post-exposure vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. World Health Organization guidance makes timing clear: treatment must begin before symptoms develop.

Myth: “Tradition” answers every safety question

It does not. Tradition cannot replace quarantine, veterinary inspection, traceability, or lawful transport. Handling sick animals, uninspected slaughter, and bite attacks create transmission risks. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. Claims about trade conditions still require named police records, court judgments, inspection findings, or official health notices.

Myth: “Farm-raised” ends accountability

A label cannot prove origin. Lawful farm production requires records, animal-health controls, transport compliance, and inspection. Without those records, buyers and communities cannot distinguish declared origin from animals moved through hidden channels. Pet theft allegations demand the same standard: verified police or court documentation, not viral claims.

Evidence must protect Vietnamese families

Vietnamese families, local advocates, veterinarians, and officials can demand a safer system without shaming communities. Household rabies exposure and commercial supply-chain failures are parallel biosecurity problems, not automatically one causal chain. Both require transparent reporting, enforceable quarantine, and accountability for illegal operators.

SDE’s demand is clear: nationwide abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
